settings-registry.description: Your GST registration type. Only regular registration is supported now.
Turn on if the prices you enter already include GST.
How each tax amount is rounded to the paisa.
Minimum HSN code length required on products.
When the tax invoice is created: when goods are dispatched (for the packed quantity), or when the order or backorder is accepted.
Round invoice totals to the nearest rupee with a round-off line.
How the invoice total is rounded to the rupee.
Default credit days for new retailers (each retailer can differ).
Accept new orders yourself, or automatically when they pass all checks.
Send the retailer an Order Confirmation (items, prices, tax estimate) when you accept an order.
Smallest order value a retailer can place. Backordered items count.
Whether the minimum order value includes GST.
What your team can change before accepting: only reduce or remove items, or also add items and increase quantities. The retailer is always notified.
Allow your staff (for example salesmen) to place orders for retailers.
Which orders and retailers sales staff can see.
Show a dashboard alert for orders not accepted within this many hours.
When backorders are off and stock runs short at checkout: stop the order and show what's short, or place only the in-stock part.
Show retailers the exact quantity in stock (otherwise only "In stock" or "Low stock").
Show a "Low stock" label to retailers when stock is at or below the reorder level.
Show products with no stock to shops, marked "Out of stock". Turn off to hide them. Applies only when backorders are off (ADR-041).
How goods receipts change a product's cost price: the average of your stock and the new bill, the latest bill cost, or never (you set it yourself) (ADR-041).
Let retailers order more than is in stock; the rest is sent when stock arrives.
When stock arrives, confirm each backorder allocation yourself, or allocate automatically (oldest orders first).
Price for backordered items sent later: the price when ordered, or today's price.
When an order would exceed a retailer's credit limit: hold it for approval, or refuse it.
Keep stock reserved for orders waiting for credit approval.
Treat a retailer as over limit when any invoice is overdue by more than this many days.
Keep extra money paid by a retailer as credit and use it for their next invoices.
Credit a cheque to the retailer's account when received (reversed automatically if it bounces) or only when it clears.
Let sales staff record payments they collect from their shops (tracked until handed over).
Age receivables by days since the invoice date, or by days past the due date.
Apply discount rules on top of a shop's special prices. Turn off to treat a special price as the final price.
When several discounts apply to a product: the best single one, add them together, or apply one after another from the most specific (ADR-038).
Shops you put on hold can still sign in and see their account, but can't order. Turn off to stop them signing in.
Show an "own brand" badge on your own-brand products in the shop (ADR-039).
Require every staff member to set up two-step verification (an authenticator app) before they can sign in.
From this time, reminders and other non-urgent WhatsApp, SMS and email messages wait until quiet hours end. In-app messages are never held.
When quiet hours end and held messages go out.
How many days a bill or receipt link sent by WhatsApp or email keeps working.
Days to remind shops of their bills: a minus number is days before the due date, the others days after it.
After the last reminder day, remind again every this many days (0: stop).
Remind salesmen of collections not handed over after this many days.
